claims.statement: I took on handoff investigation, intake-form implementation and defect follow-up for a trial approved for one library desk team; Contributor 02 retained equipment policy and approval.
claims.limits: The January proposal and February brief establish remit and approval, not deployment.

claims.statement: I traced requests through three handoffs and chose to add next-owner and return-date fields to the existing shared form instead of introducing a new application, because volunteers used a shared computer and another login would add a step.
claims.limits: The shared-computer constraint is my contemporaneous report; this does not establish that it was the only possible design.

claims.statement: My first draft wrongly combined owner and approver; after Contributor 03 explained the policy boundary, I separated the fields and acknowledged that I should have checked it before drafting.
claims.limits: Contributor 03 supplied the policy correction; I made the implementation change.

claims.statement: I implemented separate owner and approver fields, return-date validation and a printed fallback list, with Contributor 03 supplying the policy correction.
claims.limits: The implementation record alone does not prove desk use.

claims.statement: After Contributor 05 found a midnight date fault and supplied tests for both entry routes, I reproduced it, changed conversion to the desk date and tested the correction; both routes then preserved the entered date.
claims.limits: The correction was tested on the desk's two documented date-entry routes, not broader environments.

claims.statement: Contributor 04 ran the first North Desk shift and owned daily review while I handled defects; the printed fallback stayed available for the shared-computer queue.
claims.limits: This establishes the operational handoff and first-shift use, not independent volunteer operation.

claims.statement: Across two supervised shifts run by Contributor 04 and observed by Contributor 06, seven of nine return requests had a named next owner before handoff; the other two needed coordinator help.
claims.limits: There was no baseline or turnaround-time measure, and the raw-row attachment was unavailable.

claims.statement: I treated the two exceptions as evidence that a form alone did not resolve policy ambiguity, then added a visible escalation note beside the approver field instead of another status label and kept the printed fallback aligned; Contributor 03 reviewed the wording.
claims.limits: The note was implemented, but independent volunteer use had not been tested.

claims.statement: By April, the original desk team was still using the form and escalation note; Contributor 04 and the coordinator continued to run review and answer exceptions, while my return-date correction remained in place.
claims.limits: Continued use was reported for the original team only, and volunteers still needed help with exceptions.

claims.statement: The follow-up did not measure time saved and did not establish independent operation.
claims.limits: The easier-to-follow instructions were qualitative feedback, not a time or autonomy measure.

claims.statement: A second-desk trial was deferred because supervised shifts could not be staffed, while the current desk could continue; whether the form would work at another desk remained unknown.
claims.limits: The deferral reflects staffing, not a demonstrated failure of the form.

claims.statement: I offered to add return reminders if response ownership was agreed, but I had not built them.
claims.limits: This was an offer with a dependency, not an executed feature.

claims.statement: The experience changed the question I asked: instead of treating every missed handoff as something I should personally chase, I began asking whether ownership and escalation were clear enough for someone else to act, while still helping with exceptions.
claims.limits: This is my personal reflection, not a measure of team performance or a claim about a lifelong trait.

rejected_conclusions.reason: The calendar record is an invitation only and explicitly does not establish attendance, completion or a decision.

rejected_conclusions.statement: The forwarded seven-of-nine observation independently corroborates the trial result.
rejected_conclusions.reason: It is explicitly a repost of Contributor 06's observation, not a new measurement.

rejected_conclusions.statement: The unrelated Atlas catalog-index exercise is part of the equipment desk trial.
rejected_conclusions.reason: The record says it is unrelated and supplies no link.

rejected_conclusions.statement: The form was independently operated or proved time savings.
rejected_conclusions.reason: Follow-up says exceptions still required help, time saved was not measured, and supervised observations do not prove independent operation.

rejected_conclusions.statement: The second-desk deferral shows the form failed.
rejected_conclusions.reason: The recorded reason was inability to staff supervised shifts, and current-desk continuation was allowed.
